findings:
🟠 [control-list-widened-owner-stranity] MUST-FIX The diff adds 'owner@stranity.com' to CONTROL_EMAILS, a third real-domain address beyond the spec's negative-control set (the two owner emails plus foo@example.community). The scan excludes this suite file, so the entry can only serve to allowlist a literal the new catch-all flagged in another git-invoking test, and the diff converts no fixture email. Impact: the inventory now silently accepts a non-G2 address the spec says must be rewritten to @example.invalid in its own file (G11b), which defeats the catch-all for it. Smallest remediation: drop the new entry and rewrite the flagged literal to an @example.invalid address in the file where it lives, re-running that file solo; if the token is not an identity at all, use the spec's scanner-skip route (comment-only lines or self-test fixtures) and say so, rather than growing the control list.
🟡 [catchall-unspecced-skips] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The catch-all silently drops tokens whose domain ends in '.' or starts with 'pytest.', which are skips the spec does not list (it names only dollar-sign tokens, at-scoped names, comment-only lines and self-test fixtures). An address followed by a sentence period, e.g. real@owner.com., or any x@pytest.* address is never judged. Excluded from this version because no identity syntax produces such tokens and the listed-syntax pass still judges real identity spellings; a later pass could strip trailing dots and judge the rest instead of skipping.
🔵 [catchall-dollar-check-dead] CUT/FOLLOW-UP email.includes('$') can never be true because catchAllRe's character classes exclude '$', so $USER@github.com is reported as USER@github.com rather than skipped. This fails closed (a false red, not a silent pass), so it does not block; a later pass could check the character before the match for '$' or '}'.
🔵 [git-invoking-detector-duplicated] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The catch-all classifies files with its own gitInvokingRe, /(^|[\s;|&])git[\s]/, instead of reusing the inventory-two detector the spec names. Whether the two agree cannot be checked from the diff; this regex misses files whose only git calls are in $(git ...) or backticks. Excluded because such files rarely set identities and the listed-syntax pass still covers them; a later pass could share one detector.
🔵 [dq-sq-selftest-not-discriminating] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The dq-scan and sq-scan fixture lines are scanned in --files mode on a git-invoking fixture, so the catch-all would also emit those addresses and the two new assertions would pass even with the old -c user.email= pattern. They are red at base, as the spec requires, so this does not block; a later pass could assert on a fixture line with no git token.
